main_text.p: bus & conjecturis concuti & convelli so-lent, facta omnibus veri notis & characte-ribus insignita, & praeterea codicum omnium manuscriptorum & impressorum fide suffulta, nisi forte velit vir doctus animum reddere moriturae jamjam Arnaldi Sorbonici methodo qua Ecclesiae traditionem veterum subnixam testimoniis, leviffimis quibusdam rationibus evertere frustra conatus est. Nicephoro socium dedit Dallaeus Anastasium Bibliothecarium, hominem noni saeculi, Nicephoro suppa-rem, cujus haec verba adfert pag. 244. ex Praefatione Historiae Ecclesiasticae ad Ioannem Diaconum; Huic sane operi rarum duxi B. Nicephori Constantinopolitani Episcopi Chronographiam praeponere; ut scili-cet & ex ea possis aliquantula carpere, & sicubi fortasis[?] hac utendum judicaveris, tuam non lateat omnino notitiam. Deinde observat idem Dallaeus hujus Chronographiae par-tem ultimam esse illam librorum à se lau-datam stichometriam, Patriarcharum Christianorum indiculis subtextam; quam quidem stichometriam editio Anastasii Regia a. 1649. Lutetiae procurata, exhibet in calce historiae Anastasianae, ubi plane sic, ut in Graecis Nicephori, Igna-tiana in Apocryphorum Novi Testamenti censu reponuntur, ac proinde ab utroque

page.notes: The page is a continuation, so the opening paragraph is marked cont="true". The page number "13" at top right is partly worn and was read as 13. The word "fortasis" in the italic passage is set with a long-s ligature that is hard to read exactly; it is marked [?]. The faint marks along the left and right edges are edge shadow or show-through and are not transcribed. No catchword or signature is visible at the foot.
